meta.pos: verb; adj.; noun; adj.; adv.; noun; adj.; verb

defs.def: to have an idea that sth is probably true or likely to happen, especially sth bad, but without having definite proof 疑有，觉得（尤指坏事可能属实或发生）

ex.s: In Samarkand, Mr Bissell admires the architectural wonders, while on his way to Bukhara he gets a taste of police methods when suspected of drug dealing.
ex.t: 在撒马尔罕，比斯尔先生欣赏建筑奇观；而在前往布哈拉的途中，他因涉嫌贩毒而尝到了警方的手段。

defs.def: to have an idea that sb is guilty of sth, without having definite proof 怀疑（某人有罪）

ex.s: She suspected that one of her three daughters —then ten, eight, and six— had picked it up, but the girls said they hadn't.
ex.t: 她怀疑三个女儿——当时十岁、八岁和六岁——中的一个捡到了它，但女孩们说没有。

ex.s: A few years later, one of my sisters got married to a clerk—a man whom I suspect to have seen the letter—and my family celebrated by going on a rare holiday together.
ex.t: 几年后,我的一个姐妹嫁给了一个书记员——我怀疑他看到了信——和我家人一起过着罕见的节日庆祝。

ex.s: Snow suspected that the water pump was to blame.
ex.t: 斯诺怀疑水泵是罪魁祸首.

ex.s: "As I suspected, you're not Jimmy Wells," he said, impatiently with anger.
ex.t: "我怀疑你不是吉米·威尔斯,"他说,对愤怒不耐烦.

ex.s: Many people suspect that all the rock salt used every winter is harming the environment.
ex.t: 许多人怀疑每年用的所有岩盐都在危害环境。

defs.def: to be suspicious about sth; to not trust sth 怀疑；感觉有问题；不信任
that may be false and that cannot be relied on 不可信的；靠不住的
that you suspect to be dangerous or illegal 可疑的；可能有危险的；有违法嫌疑的

ex.s: It makes it easy to identify a suspect.
ex.t: 它让辨认嫌疑人变得容易。

ex.s: He pulls out a special device, points it at the suspect, and switches it on.
ex.t: 他掏出一个特殊装置，指向嫌疑人，把它打开。

ex.s: It keeps the suspect from hurting others.
ex.t: 这样可以防止嫌犯伤害他人.
